item.title: Tinubu-Shettima ticket most formidable in Nigeria’s history, says APC chair
item.description: The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Nentawe Yilwatda, has described the presidential ticket of President Bola Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima as the most formidable in Nigeria’s political history, urging Nigerians to support their re-election in 2027. Yilwatda said Tinubu deserved another term to consolidate the economic reforms and infrastructure projects initiated by his administration. He made the remarks on Saturday at the Rainbow Coalition Presidential Campaign Rally held at the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. In a statement issued by his Special Adviser on Media and Information Strategy, Abimbola Tooki, the APC chairman said the Tinubu-Shettima ticket combined political experience, courage and leadership capacity needed to address the country’s challenges. “The most formidable presidential ticket we have ever produced in Nigeria is the Tinubu-Shettima ticket. We have a candidate in President Bola Ahmed Tinubu who is fearless, courageous and determined to confront the challenges of our country. He has demonstrated the capacity to take difficult decisions in the national interest, and he has remained resolute in pursuing the transformation of Nigeria,” he said. Yilwatda defended the administration’s economic policies, including the removal of the petrol subsidy and the unification of the foreign exchange market, describing them as necessary steps towards rebuilding the economy and strengthening public finances. Although he acknowledged that the reforms had created difficulties for households and businesses, he said the government was working to cushion their effects through economic stabilisation measures, social interventions and infrastructure investments. The APC chairman also praised Tinubu’s infrastructure programme, particularly major highway projects, which he said would improve connectivity, facilitate trade and create economic opportunities. “We have a President who understands that development cannot happen without infrastructure. He has initiated an ambitious infrastructure revolution through major highway projects that will connect different parts of Nigeria, open up economic corridors, facilitate the movement of goods and services and create new opportunities for our people,” Yilwatda said. He urged Nigerians to support the continuation of the administration’s policies, arguing that a second term would allow Tinubu to consolidate the reforms and deliver their expected benefits. Turning to Rivers State, Yilwatda commended political leaders and members of the Rainbow Coalition for supporting Tinubu’s re-election bid across party lines. He said the growing political cooperation in the state reflected a shared commitment to national development, irrespective of party affiliation. “Come 2027, we want to continue with this reformer and performer as our President. item.title: UK Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch says Trump deserved midterm defeat
item.description: British Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch has said United States President Donald Trump deserved to be defeated in the midterm elections, describing the setback as “entirely self-inflicted.” In an interview with The Independent , Badenoch criticised Trump’s handling of the Iran war, his trade policies and his treatment of allies. She said his approach did not reflect conservative principles. The Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday’s midterms, flipping at least seven Senate seats and more than two dozen House districts in a major blow to Trump’s Republican Party. Asked whether Trump deserved the defeat, Badenoch replied: “Yeah. He has not been acting in the way that I would consider conservative.” She condemned his tariffs, threats towards Canada and Greenland, and disputes with allies, saying they contradicted the conservative emphasis on free markets and better trade. “Where is the push for free markets and better trade… rather than protectionism, America first, the squabbling with allies? That’s not what conservatives do,” she said. Badenoch also criticised Trump’s personal attacks on journalists and political figures, stating that his conduct fell short of the standards expected of a statesman. “Trump is very charming in person, but you see the way that he talks about journalists, about individuals. It doesn’t meet the standards a statesman should meet – always wanting to get dirty in terms of insults and so on,” she said. She expressed particular unhappiness with Trump’s remarks about British Prime Minister Keir Starmer and described his treatment of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky at the White House as “awful.” On the Iran conflict, Badenoch said she understood and supported Trump’s initial decision to take military action due to concerns about Iran acquiring nuclear weapons, but questioned the lack of a clear strategy. “We don’t want them getting nuclear weapons. But where’s the plan?” she asked. Badenoch added that she would have been content if Trump had lost the 2024 presidential election to Kamala Harris. When asked which of the two candidates she preferred, she said: “I would say I like them both equally. Make of that what you will.” She further argued that Trump had squandered the broad coalition of voters that helped him win the presidency, including increased support from Latino and Black voters. “What’s the first thing he does? Tariffs, and then talking about Greenland and Canada. A lot of people were wondering, ‘What are you doing?’” she said. Badenoch became leader of the UK Conservative Party and Leader of the Opposition in November 2024. Born Olukemi Olufunto Adegoke in London in 1980 to Nigerian parents, she previously served as Business and Trade Secretary under former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak. item.title: Okafor strike for Leeds ends Tottenham’s winning run
item.description: Leeds rode their luck to beat in-form Tottenham 1-0 on Saturday, benefiting from a controversial decision to allow Jayden Bogle to stay on the pitch after an ugly tackle on Mathys Tel. Substitute Noah Okafor was the match-winner, making an almost immediate impact after being introduced by Leeds boss Daniel Farke in the 77th minute. The home team started brightly and Spurs breathed a sigh of relief in the early minutes when VAR ruled that Mateus Fernandes had not handled the ball in the penalty area. As the first half wore on the visitors established themselves, though clear chances were at a premium. Leeds got the benefit of a contentious decision about 10 minutes before the break when Bogle caught Tel’s trailing ankle with his studs, leaving the Tottenham winger writhing on the ground in pain. After a lengthy VAR check no action was taken against Bogle, who was not even booked for the challenge, but Tel was forced off a few minutes later, hobbling off to be replaced by Dominic Solanke. Leeds had two big chances early in the second half as Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s header was blocked by Solanke before Nico Elvedi nodded wide on the follow-up. Calvert-Lewin then burst forward again but opted to pass to Ao Tanaka rather than shooting and the Japanese international skied his shot. Leeds were now on the front foot and Antonin Kinsky produced a wonderful stop after Sean Longstaff’s swivel and shot. But they got the goal their pressure deserved in the 79th minute. Harry Wilson, another substitute, controlled the ball and played it into the path of Okafor, who gave Kinsky no chance. Spurs came agonisingly close to an equaliser but goalkeeper James Trafford made a brilliant save from Jan Paul van Hecke’s header. The result ends Tottenham’s run of three straight league wins while it was the first victory in six games for Leeds, who climbed to eighth in the table. item.title: 2027: Collect campaign money, but vote your conscience, Makinde tells Nigerians
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Governor Seyi Makinde, has urged Nigerians to collect money offered to them by politicians during campaigns but vote according to their conscience. Makinde gave the advice during his presidential campaign flag-off in Bauchi, where he addressed supporters ahead of the 2027 general elections. He urged voters not to allow financial inducements to influence their electoral choices, insisting that accepting money from politicians should not translate into voting against their conscience. “When they bring money, it’s your money. Collect it, spend it, but vote your heart, and I know your heart is with us and with APM,” he told the gathering. The APM presidential candidate also called on Nigerians to support what he described as a national reset, arguing that economic hardship, insecurity and lack of inclusiveness in governance had made fundamental changes necessary. He questioned whether hunger among Nigerians should not prompt an economic reset, just as insecurity required a review of the country’s security architecture. Makinde further argued that the exclusion of many Nigerians from governance demanded a reset of the country’s socio-political environment. He said Nigerians dissatisfied with the state of affairs should embrace the proposed national reset, adding that the country needed a government capable of addressing public concerns with sincerity and transparency. He also appreciated Bauchi State Governor Bala Mohammed, whom he described as his national leader, the APM national chairman, and his wife for their support and encouragement. item.title: Any Nigerian that’s not lazy will have food on the table – Yari
item.description: Abdulaziz Yari has declared that Nigerians who are not lazy would have food on their tables. The former Zamfara governor is the Director-General of the All Progressives Congress, APC, presidential campaign council. Read Also: You would need wheelbarrow load of Naira to buy tomatoes if we didn’t act – Tinubu Yari said this on Friday during the APC’s presidential campaign rally in Uyo, the Akwa Ibom state capital. His words: “Just as I said, we have hunger. Let me ask a question here. Akwa Ibom people, from where I came from, we have food in the market. “I don’t know, in Akwa Ibom, is there any person who took his money to the market and found out there’s no rice? “You didn’t answer me. Is there anybody with money in his pocket who goes to the market to get foodstuffs and says that there’s no foodstuffs in the market? “If there’s no food in the market, that’s what we are calling hunger. But anyone who is not a lazy person, definitely he would have food on his table.” While defending President Tinubu’s economic policies, Yari cited what he described as a dip in food prices. He urged Nigerians vote Tinubu for a second term, noting that the administration’s performance should form the basis of the APC’s campaign. “As we promised Nigerians, we are going to campaign with our numbers, with what we have done for Nigerians. item.title: Five Things To Know Today
item.description: Today’s developments centre on President Tinubu’s new infrastructure commitment during his South-South campaign, fresh World Bank figures on Nigeria’s external debt, and the release of long-stranded electricity equipment. In Africa, Sudan’s humanitarian agencies warn of a serious funding shortfall. Globally, AI-related stocks have recovered some of Thursday’s losses, although investors remain concerned about technology spending and regulation. 1. Nigeria 2027: Tinubu approves Ibom Deep Seaport project during South-South campaign ﻿ What happened: President Bola Tinubu announced approval of the proposed Ibom Deep Seaport at an APC rally in Uyo on Friday, 6 November, in response to a request from Akwa Ibom Governor Umo Eno. Eno described the project as critical to the state’s maritime economy and pledged to mobilise two million votes for Tinubu’s re-election. That is a political commitment, not an electoral forecast. The president is scheduled to attend another APC rally in Port Harcourt today. Why it matters: The long-delayed seaport could expand Nigeria’s cargo-handling capacity and support manufacturing, logistics and international trade if successfully financed and constructed. Strategic implications: The announcement links an important economic infrastructure proposal with the ongoing election campaign. Presidential approval does not yet establish an agreed financing structure or construction timetable. What to watch: Formal project approval documents, funding arrangements, implementation milestones and today’s Rivers State campaign activities. 2. Nigeria economy: World Bank puts total external debt at $145 billion The World Bank headquarters in Washington, DC, on April 13, 2022. The Spring meetings will take place virtually from April 22-25. Stefani Reynolds / AFP What happened: The World Bank’s International Debt Report 2026, released on 5 November and reported extensively on Friday, shows that Nigeria’s total external debt rose by 6.6% to $145.02 billion at the end of 2025. Nigerian Debt 2024 external debt $135.99bn 2025 external debt $145.02bn Public/guaranteed 43% Private 38% Short-term 19% The total includes approximately $62.4 billion in public and publicly guaranteed obligations, $54.5 billion in private nonguaranteed debt and $28.1 billion in short-term obligations. It must not be confused with government external debt alone. Why it matters: External debt servicing is consuming more export earnings, even as some indicators of debt sustainability have improved. Business and political implications: The figures warrant careful scrutiny alongside Tinubu’s revised $7.7 billion external borrowing proposal. Borrowing costs, project productivity and fiscal transparency will remain central to the government’s economic policy debate. What to watch: Legislative scrutiny of new borrowing, financing terms, debt-service projections and independently measured returns on infrastructure spending. 3. item.title: AFCON 2027 Race: Chelle names Ndidi, Simon, Iwobi, Bassey, 21 others for Tanzania
item.description: Head Coach Éric Chelle has selected team captain Wilfred Ndidi, defenders Calvin Bassey and Semi Ajayi, midfielders Alex Iwobi and Fisayo Dele-Bashiru, and forwards Moses Simon, Ademola Lookman and Akor Adams in his 24-man roster for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying matches against Tanzania’s Taifa Stars this month. On the list as well are goalkeepers Stanley Nwabali and Arthur Okonkwo, defendes Olaoluwa Aina and Benjamin Fredricks, midfielders Tochukwu Nnadi and Samson Tijani, and forwards Moses Usor and Taiwo Awoniyi. Turkey-based defender Chibuike Nwaiwu and Czechia-based wing-back Abdullahi Bewene are also called. The Super Eagles host tournament joint-hosts Tanzania at the Godswill Akpabio Stadium in Uyo on Friday, 13th November, before flying out for the return against the Taifa Stars at Zanzibar’s Amman Stadium on Tuesday, 17th November. Nigeria, currently in second position in Group L, must win both games to improve their chances of picking the only ticket from the pool for the final tournament in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda next summer. item.title: Rivers chose Tinubu, says Wike
item.description: Nyesom Wike, Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, said the people of Rivers State have chosen President Bola Tinubu as their candidate in the January 2027 presidential election. Read Also: You would need wheelbarrow load of Naira to buy tomatoes if we didn’t act – Tinubu Wike said this on Saturday while welcoming Tinubu and his delegation to the Adokiye Amiesimaka Stadium in Port Harcourt for the president’s campaign rally. He is the coordinator of the presidential campaign council in the state. Wike said: “Your Excellency, this is Rivers State’s rally. We did not mobilise anybody from any other state. You can see with your eyes that the people of Rivers State have already concluded and agreed that on January 16, they will vote for you. “Since the inception of democracy in 1999, Rivers people have never had it this way. We have no less than 47 political appointments from Mr President. “So, who is our brother? Our brother is Bola Ahmed Tinubu because he has identified with the people of Rivers state. He described President Tinubu as a political ally of Rivers people, saying the president had demonstrated his commitment to the state through federal projects and political appointments. Also, Wike took a swipe at Rotimi Amaechi’s projects. He questioned the outcome of an alleged fumigation exercise in Rivers, saying it had failed to eliminate mosquitoes. “All we are saying to the vice-presidential candidate is, please, come and give an account of how you fumigated Rivers state. You fumigated Rivers state so that there would be no mosquitoes. “Have mosquitoes gone? Are mosquitoes not biting you?” He recalled Amaechi’s role as director-general of the presidential campaigns of former President Muhammadu Buhari. Wike said the then APC candidate failed to secure up to 15 percent of the votes in Rivers state in the 2015 and 2019 presidential elections. item.title: FG warns public against NTI admissions, cancels 2026 NCE, degree intake
item.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Ministry of Education has warned prospective students, parents and the general public against seeking admission into unauthorised National Certificate in Education (NCE) and degree programmes at the National Teachers’ Institute (NTI), Kaduna, following regulatory breaches involving admissions, accreditation and university affiliations. Consequently, all admissions into NTI’s NCE and degree programmes for the 2026 academic session have been cancelled, while the Institute has been directed to discontinue all university affiliations and degree-awarding arrangements, as it is not authorised to award NCE and university degrees. The ministry, in a statement by its Director, Press and Public Relations, Boriowo Folasade, emphasised that no further admissions into the affected programmes, whether full-time, part-time or through Distance Learning Studies (DLS), are permitted. Members of the public are therefore strongly advised not to apply, accept admission offers or make payments for such programmes. According to the statement, “The directive follows violations of the Ministerial Operational Guidelines issued on 12 September 2025. The Ministry clarifies that NCE admissions must comply with applicable Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) requirements and accreditation standards of the National Commission for Colleges of Education (NCCE).” “The National Universities Commission (NUC) is also to notify affected universities and ensure compliance with the directive on NTI’s discontinued degree-awarding arrangements,” the statement added. “To protect innocent students already enrolled, the NCCE will conduct comprehensive accreditation of existing NCE II–IV Distance Learning programmes and study centres across the six geopolitical zones. Eligible students may complete their programmes, subject to accreditation outcomes and regulatory requirements, “it further added. The ministry reiterated that NTI’s statutory mandate remains teacher training, retraining, in-service development and continuous professional development. This includes pedagogical capacity-building and the three-to-six-month Special Abridged Programme for serving teachers with non-education degrees to acquire the professional competencies required for registration with the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN), subject to applicable regulations. The ministry stressed that the intervention is intended to protect students, uphold academic standards and prevent further exposure of prospective applicants to unapproved programmes. It urged the public to verify programme accreditation and admission status through relevant regulatory authorities and official government channels before making enrolment or payment decisions. item.title: Makinde: Tinubu’s poor planning plunged millions of Nigerians into hardship
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has blamed the economic hardship facing millions of Nigerians on what he described as inadequate planning by the President Bola Tinubu-led administration. Makinde said major economic policy decisions introduced by the Federal Government were implemented without adequate plans and frameworks to cushion their effects on citizens, thereby worsening the economic difficulties faced by Nigerians. The APM presidential candidate spoke on Friday during a live interview on the Bauchi Radio Corporation (BRC), while in Bauchi State to flag off his 2027 presidential campaign. He argued that the immediate impact of the administration’s economic policies on Nigerians was a consequence of taking major decisions without adequate preparation and effective implementation strategies. Makinde stressed that economic reforms must be supported by proper planning and clear implementation frameworks to ensure that ordinary citizens do not bear the brunt of government policies. He said addressing the country’s economic challenges would require fundamental structural reforms and strong political will. The Oyo governor also highlighted the APM’s Reset Nigeria Agenda, which he said was designed to address the country’s challenges through a documented policy framework and the party’s manifesto. According to him, the agenda focuses on reforming critical sectors of the economy, promoting sustainable development and restoring true federalism that recognises and respects Nigeria’s diverse nationalities. item.title: Explainer: Who won 2023 presidential 2023 in Kaduna, Katsina – the 161,829 votes difference
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi – ABUJA Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, won Katsina State in the February 25, 2023 presidential election by only 6,762 votes over Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC, according to results declared by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC. Read Also: * Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal * How Buhari promised me APC presidential ticket in 2022; I regret listening to him – Amaechi He also won neighbouring Kaduna State, where his lead was far wider. Katsina: a margin of 6,762 votes Atiku polled 489,045 votes in Katsina, against Tinubu’s 482,283. Out of 1,058,673 valid votes, that is a gap of about 0.64 of a percentage point. Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party, NNPP, came third with 69,386 votes. Peter Obi, who ran on the Labour Party, LP, ticket, had just 6,376 votes. Katsina had 3,516,719 registered voters. The 1,058,673 valid votes represent about 30 per cent of that figure. Kaduna: a lead of 155,067 votes Kaduna was not close. Atiku scored 554,360 votes to Tinubu’s 399,293, a lead of 155,067. Obi came third in Kaduna with 294,494 votes, and Kwankwaso was fourth with 92,969. The state had 4,335,208 registered voters, of whom 1,418,046 were accredited. INEC recorded 1,360,153 valid votes and 41,223 rejected votes, making 1,401,376 votes cast in total. Where the two states differ Obi’s vote shows the sharpest contrast. He polled 294,494 votes in Kaduna. But he got only 6,376 in Katsina, where he finished fourth behind Kwankwaso. Across both states, Atiku polled 1,043,405 votes and Tinubu 881,576, giving Atiku a combined lead of 161,829. Obi had 300,870 votes and Kwankwaso 162,355. Nearly all of Atiku’s combined lead came from Kaduna. Katsina added only 6,762 votes to it. item.title: Kalu urges Igbo leaders to unite, engage in Nigerian politics
item.description: Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, has urged Igbo elders, leaders and stakeholders to unite and take a more active role in Nigeria’s politics, warning that disunity and political apathy have weakened the South-East’s influence in national affairs. The call was contained in a statement issued on Saturday by his Chief Press Secretary, Levinus Nwabughiogu. Kalu also called for a change of mindset among Igbo people, particularly those who have traditionally focused on developing their communities while keeping away from national politics. He made the call on Friday at the South-East Stakeholders’ Convergence, also known as the South-East Elders and Stakeholders Meeting, held at the Imo State Government House, Owerri. The meeting, convened to discuss unity, peace and development in Igbo land, was chaired by a former Military Governor of Imo State and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Senator Ike Nwachukwu. Kalu, who represents Bende Federal Constituency of Abia State, said unity was essential to the political relevance and development of the South-East, stressing that the region could achieve more if its leaders and people worked towards common goals. “Unity is strength. We will achieve more when we are united. The need for unity cannot be overemphasised. Peace leads to the development of communities,” he said. Commending the elders and stakeholders for attending the meeting despite their individual engagements, the Deputy Speaker described their gathering as an expression of patriotism and commitment to the progress of Igbo land. He said their example would encourage younger generations to sustain the quest for unity and development, likening leadership to a relay race in which older generations hand over the baton to their successors. Kalu, however, warned that the Igbo people risked losing their heritage and political direction if they continued to operate in isolation. On the region’s political influence, he said the numerical strength of the Igbo was not adequately reflected in the political fortunes of the five South-East states, partly because many people from the region lived in other parts of the country. He argued that a common political agenda would enable the Igbo to consolidate their strength and make their voices more influential in national decision-making. “The number of votes of Ndi Igbo is not what we are getting across the five states because we are scattered around the country. If we take a position now and say, Igbo, this is our agenda, this is what we want to do, I can assure you, the whole of Nigeria will feel our impact,” he said. The Deputy Speaker also urged the people to abandon what he described as the post-civil war mindset of avoiding national politics and concentrating solely on developing their communities. item.title: Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, ABUJA Lagos, Oyo and Osun states each backed a different candidate in the February 25, 2023 presidential election, according to the results declared by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC. Read Also: How Buhari promised me APC presidential ticket in 2022; I regret listening to him – Amaechi Peter Obi of the Labour Party, LP, won Lagos; Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC, won Oyo, and Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, won Osun. What happened in Lagos? Lagos produced the closest of the three contests. Obi polled 582,454 votes (45.81 per cent), while Tinubu, the APC candidate, followed with 572,606 votes (45.04 per cent). The gap was 9,848 votes, less than one percentage point. Atiku trailed far behind with 75,750 votes (5.96 per cent), and Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party, NNPP, had 8,442 votes (0.66 per cent). What happened in Oyo? Oyo was not close. Tinubu polled 449,884 votes (55.58 per cent), well ahead of Atiku’s 182,977 votes (22.60 per cent). His lead of 266,907 votes was the widest of the three states. Obi came third in Oyo with 99,110 votes (12.24 per cent), and Kwankwaso had 4,095 votes (0.51 per cent). What happened in Osun? Osun was nearly as tight as Lagos. Atiku won with 354,366 votes (46.88 per cent), while Tinubu had 343,945 votes (45.50 per cent), a difference of 10,421 votes. Obi finished third with 23,283 votes, and Kwankwaso had 713 votes (0.09 per cent). What the combined figures show Added together, the results tell a story that the three winners alone do not. Tinubu won only one of the states, yet he finished first or second in all three and polled 1,366,435 votes across them. Obi, who topped the Lagos poll, totalled 704,847 votes across the three states because he fell to third in both Oyo and Osun. Atiku polled 613,093 votes, and Kwankwaso finished fourth in each state, with 13,250 votes combined. Put differently, Obi’s win came by the thinnest of margins in the most populous of the three states. But Tinubu’s lead in Oyo was large enough to leave him comfortably ahead of both rivals on the combined tally. item.title: Pope Leo begins South America tour in ‘fairly good shape’
item.description: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Uruguay, where he will celebrate a Mass on Saturday, as he began a 12-day tour of South America in “fairly good shape.” Leo’s sixth international tour takes him to the continent that helped shape his priesthood, just three weeks after surgery for a tumor on his right lung. The 71-year-old pontiff will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on one of the most intense papal trips in decades, meeting political leaders, prisoners and the poor, as well as old friends. Thousands of people, some waving yellow-and-white Vatican flags, lined the seafront of Uruguay’s capital Montevideo to greet him as he waved from a custom-made popemobile. But the crowds were relatively sparse in Latin America’s most secular country compared with Leo’s recent visits to France and Spain. Speaking in a half-empty Plaza Independencia, after being welcomed by left-wing President Yamandu Orsi, the pope lamented Uruguay’s high suicide rates — among the highest in the world — and appealed for healthcare to be “accessible to everyone.” He said the care he received after his lung cancer diagnosis made him think of the “many men and women who lack the means to obtain a timely diagnosis” or receive treatment. Leo will celebrate Mass on Saturday in a park in Paysandu, a city in western Uruguay, where 30,000 pilgrims are expected. He will then return to Montevideo to visit Casavalle, the neighborhood with the highest homicide rate in the capital, as well as the Catholic University and the Centenario Stadium, where he will preside over a prayer vigil for 60,000 people. Leo’s visit to Uruguay is the first to the country by a pope in nearly four decades. – In ‘fairly good shape’ – He told reporters on the plane carrying him across the Atlantic he was “in fairly good shape” following his surgery, and his advice for others facing their own cancer diagnosis was “not to be afraid.” The pontiff said he was bringing a message of “hope” to the world’s most Catholic continent. Liberal Uruguay is at odds with the Catholic Church — as well as Latin America’s new crop of conservative leaders — on issues such as same-sex marriage, abortion and euthanasia, which was legalized there last year. Leo issued a call for the “protection of the unborn” but also spoke about issues specific to Uruguay, such as its high suicide rates, which he called “painful.” A committed environmentalist, he had praise for the small country’s “remarkable” achievement in greening its economy, which runs mainly on renewables. – ‘One of my many homes’ – The highlight of his tour will be Peru, where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary and which he has referred to as “one of my many homes.” The Church’s first US-born pope, who has repeatedly clashed with President Donald Trump over the Middle East war, spoke on his plane about voting in this week’s US midterm elections. item.title: You would need wheelbarrow load of Naira to buy tomatoes if we didn’t act – Tinubu
item.description: President Bola Tinubu said that Naira would have been so worthless, it would be moved about by wheelbarrow if not for his economic policies that moved Nigeria away from the brink of financial collapse. Read Also: Tinubu to Nigerians: ‘I promise better future’ Tinubu, the presidential candidate of All Progressives Congress, APC, said this during his visit to Akwa Ibom State, where he urged voters to support his administration and Governor Umo Eno. He described the January 16, 2027 election as consequential, saying it would determine the country’s direction. Defending his economic policies, Tinubu said his administration had moved Nigeria away from the brink of financial collapse. According to him, “This coming election, on January 16th is a consequential election. It will define the direction of this country. “When I took over, 27 governors out of 36 of this country were unable to pay salary, not to talk of pension, and gratuity. Today, I can say that we are out of that tunnel. “And I can beat my chest to say we are out of the despair, the dark tunnel of uncertainty and the calamity of a possible bankruptcy. “By now if we didn’t take over, if we didn’t do what we did, we will be using the wheelbarrows to move our naira about because it will have become valueless. “We are talking of 1,300 now to a dollar because it still has pocketable value. If we had left it, it would have been a wheelbarrow when you go to the market to buy tomatoes. That is the truth.” On young voters The President urged the electorate, particularly young people, to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards, PVCs. He described it as their most potent instrument for determining the country’s political future. At a reception held in his honour at Ibom Palm Resort, Tinubu praised Eno. He described the resort as evidence of purposeful leadership and the possibility of reclaiming environmentally degraded land for productive use. “We are standing on a resort to the glory of God. It is a product of 73 acres of land of gully erosion, reclaimed, surrounded with a good, romantic, artificial lake, demonstrating a serious vision that is achievable when honest people are working for their homes,” he said. item.title: Stephanie Okechukwu: World’s tallest women’s college basketball player makes her debut
item.description: It is a new era for women’s college basketball after Thursday night’s debut of 7-foot-1, 21-year-old Nigerian Stephanie Okechukwu at Texas Tech . She is world’s tallest women’s college basketball player. Texas Tech center Stephanie Okechukwu scored six points in her debut as women´s college basketball´s tallest player at 7-foot-1. The 21-year-old freshman scored her first points on a pair of free throws and added 10 rebounds and three blocks in 21 minutes in a season-opening 64-37 win over Charlotte on Thursday night, the DailyMail reports. Destinee Hooks led the Lady Raiders with 16 points. Texas Tech coach Krista Gerlich believes there´s still much room for Okechukwu to grow as a player. “She does not think she played well,” Gerlich said. “I´m excited for her and it´s only going to get better. There is definitely more.” Okechukwu is from Nigeria and eclipses the previously tallest players listed at 6-10 – Middle Tennessee State freshman Nicole Dominguez and Eastern Illinois sophomore Abbie Boutilier. Okechukwu signed with Texas Tech in January but did not play last season. After completing her high school career in Japan in 2024, she split time playing in an AAU league in the Philippines and training in Nigeria. She was initially limited to just two years of college eligibility because she took what was considered a gap year off before the NCAA granted her four years after Texas Tech filed an appeal for a waiver. item.title: Lagos ranks 28th among world’s 50 most dangerous cities – Survey
item.description: By Sola Ogundipe Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial nerve centre and one of Africa’s busiest megacities, has been ranked among the world’s 50 most dangerous cities in 2026, placing 28th on a global crime index that raises fresh questions about urban safety, insecurity and the growing pressure on law enforcement. Lagos is the only Nigerian city on the ranking published by the “Numbeo Crime Index by City 2026” – a Serbia-based global data platform that compiles crowd-sourced information on crime safety, cost of living and quality of life across cities and countries. The list records Lagos with a crime index of 68.8, placing it in the high crime category under Numbeo’s classification. The index ranges from zero to 100, with scores above 60 classified as high and those above 80 as very high. Nigeria’s commercial capital is placed ahead of major cities including Damascus in Syria, New Orleans in the United States, San Juan in Puerto Rico and Santo Domingo in the Dominican Republic. According to the survey, five South African cities occupy positions among the top eight, with Pietermaritzburg taking the first position, followed by Pretoria in second place, Johannesburg in fifth, Durban in sixth and Port Elizabeth in eighth. Caracas, Venezuela, and Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea, occupy third and fourth positions respectively. Windhoek, Namibia, comes in at number 30. The figures also point to persistent safety concerns across the Americas. Brazil has five cities among the top 25, while the United States has several, including Memphis, Detroit, Baltimore, Albuquerque and St. Louis. Other cities featured in the top 50 include Kingston in Jamaica, Mexico City, Marseille in France, Manila in the Philippines, Birmingham in the United Kingdom and Houston in the United States. Numbeo’s Crime Index draws on several indicators, among them residents’ perceptions of crime, how safe they feel walking alone during the day or at night, and their experiences or concerns about robbery, mugging, car theft, burglary, physical attacks and harassment. It also considers drug-related problems, property crime, violent crime and corruption. The ranking reflects perceptions captured by Numbeo’s survey, rather than a verified ranking of reported criminal offences. It is based on surveys completed by Numbeo website visitors and not a direct count of police-recorded offences, reported criminal incidents or official national crime statistics. Numbeo processes the responses into scores ranging from zero to 100 to make comparisons between cities possible. The organisation also acknowledges that public perceptions of crime may not always correspond with official crime figures. For Lagos, the survey notes that the 28th position adds to the concerns surrounding safety in one of Africa’s most populous urban centres. item.title: What do Airtel, Fidelity bank and Lekki Gardens have in common?
item.description: By Temiloluwa Johnson A telecoms giant, a bank and a property developer. On paper, nothing. On ARCON’s honours list, quite a lot. A telecoms giant, a bank and a property developer. On paper, nothing. On ARCON’s honours list, quite a lot. One connects millions of phone calls a day. One looks after people’s money. One builds homes. It is hard to think of three Nigerian businesses with less to do with each other. Yet on Friday, 23 October, Airtel, Fidelity Bank and Lekki Gardens found themselves on the same list. At the ARCON Special Recognition Awards (ASRA) 2026, held at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Sheraton Hotel, Ikeja, the Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria honoured a small group of advertisers for compliance. Lekki Gardens was recognised in the Real Estate and Properties category, alongside honourees that included CocaCola, Peak, Moniepoint and Chicken Republic in their own sectors. So what do they have in common? Not size, and not industry. What they share is a record. None of them entered. ARCON’s Secretariat went back through every eligible advertisement it had vetted in the period under review and picked out the advertisers with the highest volumes of approved work in each sector. A technical assessment followed, then a jury, then final ratification, with an independent audit firm checking the process from start to finish. Nobody could buy, pitch or charm their way onto that list. The only way on was to keep getting it right. There is a second thing the three share, and it is the more important one. Each of them is trusted with something people cannot afford to lose. For Airtel, it is the connection. For Fidelity Bank, it is the savings. For Lekki Gardens, it is usually both, because a home is the largest financial decision most families will ever make. That is why the company treats its adverts as promises rather than slogans. “Compliance here is not a department. It is in the DNA of the business,” says Mr Oluwole Ntia, Lekki Gardens’ Group Head of Marketing Operations, who received the award. “We do things well, do things right and protect the resources our customers entrust to us.” Founder Dr Richard Nyong has said the same thing for years, in fewer words: “If the customer does not choose you, you do not get paid.” So, what do Airtel, Fidelity Bank and Lekki Gardens have in common? When the regulator went looking for the advertisers it could hold up as the standard, it found all three. item.title: The Records Are On The Ballot
item.description: The campaign has acquired a sharper edge: In Akwa Ibom Today, President Bola Tinubu challenged the leadership credentials of his principal opponents. His apparent references to Peter Obi’s handling of erosion in Anambra and Atiku Abubakar’s departure from the PDP sought to turn their past decisions into questions about their fitness to govern. These were campaign accusations, rather than independently established assessments of their records. Vice-President Kashim Shettima reinforced the attack, questioning Obi’s credibility and arguing that Atiku’s experience should be judged by accomplishments rather than years in office. His assertion that Obi has lost goodwill remains a partisan assessment; it does not establish a measurable change in voter support. The political intention is clear: put the challengers on the defensive. That matters for an incumbent whose own performance is under examination. If voters spend more time debating whether the opposition is credible, the government gains room to argue that continuity is the safer choice. But scrutiny travels both ways. Once the campaign becomes a comparison of records, Tinubu must also answer for the results of his presidency: purchasing power, security, employment and public services. UYO: Projects and Political Persuasion Today’s visit combined the inauguration of projects executed by Governor Umo Eno’s administration with a political gathering. It gave Tinubu a setting in which visible infrastructure and electoral advocacy could reinforce each other. The distinction between state projects and federal achievements still matters. Political cooperation can support delivery, but credit should follow the evidence about funding, execution and responsibility. For the governing camp, the opportunity is to connect infrastructure with an argument about competent government. For voters, the question is how those investments improve transport, commerce, services and livelihoods. An inauguration provides a powerful picture. Its electoral value depends on the public’s experience after the ceremony. ATIKU: Defiance Needs a Legal Foundation Atiku’s response today remained combative. In a statement, he accused the government of using the courts to evade electoral judgment and reaffirmed his intention to challenge the ruling. That allegation requires attribution; it is not proof of government direction of the proceedings. His campaign also continued in Kebbi on Thursday, despite the judgment. Reporting published today describes promises on security, employment and restoring fuel subsidies. The event should therefore be treated as yesterday’s campaign activity, rather than a fresh Friday rally. Politically, continuing to campaign signals resolve. item.title: 2027: Opposition’s battle for space
item.description: Within a span of one week, opposition political parties in Nigeria have experienced various challenges in their bid to contest in the 2027 general elections. From the bids for the presidency to governorship, national assembly and state assembly seats, opposition candidates have not been finding it easy to campaign as they wish as they are faced with various forms of harassment, suppression and intimidation. Weekend Trust reports that 31 states in the country are under the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) while two of the remaining five opposition governors have been included in the presidential campaign council of the party. Our correspondents recall that within the week, the convoy of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) was attacked in Cross Rivers State, while the bid by the African Democratic Congress (ADC) to hold a rally in Sokoto met with stiff opposition and in Edo and Plateau States, the billboards of major opposition candidates were pulled down. Justice Peter Lifu, in a judgement, nullified the emergence of the former Senate President, David Mark, Rauf Aregbesola and others as national officers of the ADC. The judge held that the nominations of candidates for the 2027 general elections were cancelled on account of emerging from an “illegal and unlawful leadership.” In the same day, the presidential campaign convoy of the ADC was reportedly attacked in Kebbi State, as the candidate, Atiku, moved through Kebbi on campaign engagements on Thursday. According to reports from the campaign team, thugs blocked the convoy and pelted vehicles with stones. These developments, according to political observers, represent a systematic weakening of opposition parties and raise concerns over Nigeria’s democracy. Due to the frequency in occurrence, opposition figures and civil society organisations have accused the ruling party, APC, of utilizing state-backed coercion, judicial manipulation, and targeted inducements to systematically dismantle counter-balancing political structures across the country. Critics warn that by neutralising alternative political platforms ahead of upcoming electoral cycles, the APC-led administration is actively eroding the essential checks and balances required for democratic accountability. Efforts to get the ruling party (APC) at the national level to respond to the allegations proved abortive as the National Publicity Secretary of the party, Felix Morka, did not respond to phone calls or WhatsApp messages sent to him.
